instructions:
Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 385 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

Dear Principal,

I heard you are thinking about changing the cell phone policy and I think Policy 1 is the better one. Students should be able to bring phones to school and use them at lunch and free periods, as long as they are off during class.

My first reason is safety. A lot of parents want to be able to reach their kids during the day, and kids need a way to call home if plans change. Like if practice gets cancelled or you feel sick, you can just send a quick text. If there was a real emergency like a lockdown or a bus accident, a phone could let your family know your okay. If you ban phones completely parents would be way more worried.

My second reason is that Policy 1 teaches us to be responsible. In a few years we are going to be in college or have jobs and nobody is going to take our phones away. We will have to decide on our own when to put them down. If we can use phones at lunch but have to keep them off in class, we get practice at that. A total ban just teaches kids to sneak them.

Third, a full ban would be really hard to enforce. Kids are still going to bring phones in their pockets and backpacks, and teachers will waste time searching and taking them instead of teaching. With Policy 1 the rule is clear and fair so most kids will actually follow it. Teachers only have to do something if a phone comes out in class.

Last, phones can be helpful during free time. You can check your assignments online, look stuff up for a project, or text your group partners. Lunch is also supposed to be a time to relax, and listening to music or texting your mom for a few minutes doesn't hurt anybody.

Some people think phones will distract students. I get that, but Policy 1 already fixes that by making phones stay off when we are learning. If someone breaks the rule they can get in trouble, and everyone else still gets the benefits.

For all these reasons I hope you pick Policy 1. It keeps students safe, teaches responsibility, and it is easier to enforce.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
